headline: Revenue rose 29%, 48% and 86% in Q1-Q3 FY2026 as AI semiconductors led; all four theses hold, with customer financing the new risk.
summary: Broadcom's first three fiscal quarters of FY2026 (ended January 31, May 3 and August 2, 2026) brought revenue of $71,089 million, up 55% on the prior-year period of $45,872 million [1][2]. Semiconductor revenue grew 52%, 79% and 127% in the three quarters, and AI semiconductor revenue reached $16.7 billion in Q3, up 221% [1]. Gross margin stayed between 68% and 70%, at 69% in Q3 [2]. Free cash flow was $13,665 million in Q3, or 46% of revenue [1]. All four theses are intact or strengthened against their signposts. The open point is software: segment revenue grew 1% in Q1 and 9% in Q2, and the releases reviewed do not give the software operating income that the T2 signpost requires [1]. The new risk is customer financing. In June 2026 Broadcom launched the AI XPV platform with a first tranche of $35 billion and a backstop with a maximum undiscounted exposure of about $29 billion [2]. Consensus FY2026 revenue is $105,981 million and FY2027 EPS is $19.33, at 24.5x forward earnings [3].
results_commentary:
Q1 FY2026 (ended January 31, 2026) was the first step-up. Revenue rose 29% to $19,311 million against $14,916 million a year earlier, and GAAP operating income rose to $8,563 million from $6,260 million [1][2]. Semiconductor revenue grew 52% to $12,515 million, and AI revenue of $8.4 billion grew 106% [1]. Software was the weak line: revenue rose 1% to $6,796 million [1]. The releases do not explain the software result. Gross margin was 68%, flat against 68% a year earlier, because the 10-Q says the gain from revenue growth was offset by a higher mix of semiconductor revenue [2]. Products revenue includes $1,755 million of upfront license revenue in Q1, which lifts the reported figure and is not a recurring run-rate [2].

Q2 FY2026 (ended May 3, 2026) accelerated. Revenue rose 48% to $22,187 million, above the approximately $22.0 billion guided in March [1][2]. Semiconductor revenue grew 79% to $15,009 million, and AI revenue of $10.8 billion grew 143% [1]. Software revenue grew 9% to $7,178 million, the weakest of the three quarters for that segment [1]. Gross margin rose to 69% from 68%, the first clear gain in the year-on-year comparison [2]. GAAP operating income was $10,788 million against $5,829 million, and the operating margin moved to 49% from 39% [2]. Customer concentration eased from Q1 but stayed above the prior year: the top five end customers accounted for about 45% of net revenue, against 50% in Q1 and 40% a year earlier [2].

Q3 FY2026 (ended August 2, 2026) was the strongest quarter. Revenue rose 86% to $29,591 million, and AI semiconductor revenue grew 221% to $16.7 billion, up 54% from Q2 [1]. Semiconductor revenue reached $20,839 million, up 127%. Software revenue rose 29% to $8,752 million, the fastest growth of the three quarters, but the release does not state the cause [1]. Gross margin was 69% against 67% a year earlier [2]. GAAP operating income was $15,955 million against $5,887 million [1]. Free cash flow was $13,665 million, up 95% [1]. Three items moved the wrong way. Days sales outstanding rose to 42 from 37 a year earlier [3]. The diluted share count rose to 4,774 million from 4,722 million, a 1.1% increase over the year [3]. Buybacks fell from $7.85 billion in Q1 to $0.6 billion in Q2, and the Q3 10-Q highlights list no common stock repurchase, only $5,641 million of senior note repurchases [2]. Net debt fell to $35,444 million from $53,511 million a year earlier [3]. Q4 guidance is $34.8 billion of revenue, up 93%, at a non-GAAP operating margin of 66%, down from the 67% guided for Q3 [1].

thesis_check.thesis: T1: AI demand keeps semiconductor revenue growing fast enough to support consensus FY2026 revenue of about $106 billion.
thesis_check.signpost: Semiconductor revenue growth of at least 40% year on year in the fiscal 2026 10-K, due by early December 2026. Interim invalidation: growth below 20% in any fiscal 2026 quarter, or a cut in FY2026 consensus revenue beyond the level set in the annual report.
thesis_check.evidence: Semiconductor revenue grew 52% to $12,515 million in Q1, 79% to $15,009 million in Q2 and 127% to $20,839 million in Q3 [1]. Year-to-date revenue of $71,089 million plus the $34.8 billion Q4 guide sums to about $105.9 billion (illustrative sum), in line with FY2026 consensus of $105,981 million, so no consensus cut has occurred [1][2][3].

thesis_check.thesis: T2: Infrastructure software keeps its high margin as the subscription transition continues.
thesis_check.signpost: Software operating income growth of at least 25% in the fiscal 2026 10-K, due by early December 2026. Invalidation: software operating income growth below the 10% level set in the annual report.
thesis_check.evidence: Software segment revenue grew 1% to $6,796 million in Q1 and 9% to $7,178 million in Q2, the two slowest quarters, and then 29% to $8,752 million in Q3 [1]. The releases and 10-Qs reviewed do not give software segment operating income, so the signpost cannot yet be tested directly [1][2].

thesis_check.thesis: T3: Gross margin holds near 68% even as AI rack sales grow, so the margin expansion lasts.
thesis_check.signpost: Reported gross margin of at least 66% in each fiscal 2026 quarter. Invalidation: quarterly gross margin below 63%, the fiscal 2024 level.
thesis_check.evidence: Gross margin was 68% in Q1 (flat year on year), 69% in Q2 (68% a year earlier) and 69% in Q3 (67% a year earlier), above the 66% signpost [2][3]. The 10-Q attributes the Q1 flatness to a higher mix of semiconductor revenue, so the rack-driven margin compression the filing warned of has not appeared yet [2].

thesis_check.thesis: T4: Earnings estimates keep rising, so the current valuation stays supported by consensus rather than requiring a higher growth rate.
thesis_check.signpost: FY2027 EPS consensus holds at or above $19 through the fiscal 2026 10-K, due by early December 2026. Invalidation: FY2027 EPS consensus cut by more than the level set in the annual report, or the stock trades above 40x forward earnings without an earnings upgrade.
thesis_check.evidence: All four recent quarters beat EPS consensus, by 1.3% in the January quarter, 1.7% in the April quarter and 2.5% in the July quarter [3]. FY2027 EPS consensus is $19.33, down 1.0% over 90 days, with 2 raises and no cuts in the last 30 days, and forward P/E is 24.5x, well below the 40x trigger [3]. The consensus figures are a single snapshot dated after the Q3 release, so the per-quarter status rests on the beats and this snapshot [3].

risk_update: Customer concentration rose from the prior year. The top five end customers were about 50% of net revenue in Q1 and about 45% in Q2, against 40% in each year-ago quarter, and one distributor customer accounted for 42% of net revenue in Q1 and Q2 against 29% a year earlier [2]. The Q3 concentration figure was not in the extracted 10-Q text. The AI XPV platform, launched in June 2026 with a $35 billion first tranche, adds a contingent liability: Broadcom's backstop on customer lease obligations has a maximum undiscounted exposure of about $29 billion, with no amounts paid so far [2]. This makes the customer-financing risk named in the 10-K concrete. Margin risk from AI racks has not yet appeared in reported gross margin, which rose to 69% in Q2 and Q3 [2][3]. Net debt eased: $35,444 million at the Q3 balance sheet date against $48,958 million at fiscal year-end, helped by $5,641 million of senior note repurchases in Q3 [2][3]. Share count dilution is a new point of watch, since the diluted count rose 1.1% over the year while buybacks slowed [3].
outlook: Q4 FY2026 guidance is $34.8 billion of revenue, up 93%, and a non-GAAP operating margin of about 66%, which matches the 66% of the year-earlier quarter [1]. Year-to-date revenue plus the Q4 guide sums to about $105.9 billion (illustrative), in line with FY2026 consensus of $105,981 million [1][3]. Consensus FY2026 EPS is $11.65, up 0.3% over 90 days, and FY2027 EPS is $19.33, down 1.0% over 90 days [3]. The reverse DCF implies 26.6% annual revenue growth for ten years, against FY2027 consensus revenue growth of 64.8% [2][3]. An illustrative IRR of 19.3% assumes the consensus path is delivered [3]. What would prove the view wrong: semiconductor growth below 20% in any quarter, a cut in FY2027 EPS consensus beyond the invalidation level in the annual report [4], or a software operating income gain below the baseline threshold in the 10-K. The fiscal 2026 10-K, due in early December 2026, is the next test of T1, T2 and T4.
